title: Ratio of Gaussian tail logarithms
statement: Let $0<\rho<1$, let $Q(t)=\mathbb{P}(Z>t)$ for a standard normal random variable $Z$, and set $B_\rho(t)=Q((t-1)/\rho)$. As $t\to+\infty$, $\frac{\log B_\rho(t)}{\log Q(t)}$ tends to $\frac{1}{\rho^2}$.
